from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Imagine a smoothie made of many different fruits.',
            'It looks complex, but it is just a mixture.',
            'The Fourier Transform is a magic deconstruction machine.',
            'It separates the smoothie back into individual fruit piles.',
            'It decomposes complex signals into simple waves.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Smoothie Analogy: Deconstruction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Helper for a simple complex wave
        def get_complex_wave(time_val):
            return FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * (x - time_val)) + 
                          0.2 * np.sin(4 * PI * (x - time_val)) + 
                          0.1 * np.sin(6 * PI * (x - time_val)),
                x_range=[0, 3],
                color=WHITE
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        complex_wave = get_complex_wave(0)
        self.place_in_area(complex_wave, "A1", "B3")
        
        def update_wave(mob):
            new_wave = get_complex_wave(time_tracker.get_value())
            new_wave.match_points(mob)
            # Center it back to area
            mob.move_to(self.grid["A2"] + DOWN * 0.4) 

        complex_wave.add_updater(update_wave)
        
        self.play(Create(complex_wave))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        machine_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.2)
        machine_label = Text("Fourier Machine", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        machine_label.next_to(machine_box, UP, buff=0.1)
        machine_group = VGroup(machine_box, machine_label)
        self.place_in_area(machine_group, "C2", "D3")
        
        decomposition_text = Text("Decomposition", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(decomposition_text, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(machine_group), FadeIn(decomposition_text))
        
        # Complex wave flows into the machine
        self.play(
            complex_wave.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(machine_group.get_center()),
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(6),
            run_time=2
        )
        complex_wave.remove_updater(update_wave)
        self.play(FadeOut(complex_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Pure sine waves emerging
        wave_red = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[0, 1.5], color="#FF0000")
        wave_green = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(4 * PI * x), x_range=[0, 1.5], color="#00FF00")
        wave_blue = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(6 * PI * x), x_range=[0, 1.5], color="#0000FF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(wave_red, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_green, "C5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(wave_blue, "D5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Fruit placeholders (Represented by colored circles since assets aren't provided)
        strawberry = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        banana = Ellipse(width=0.3, height=0.1, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).rotate(PI/4)
        blueberry = Circle(radius=0.1, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(strawberry, "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(banana, "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(blueberry, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        fruits = VGroup(strawberry, banana, blueberry)
        output_waves = VGroup(wave_red, wave_green, wave_blue)
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                AnimationGroup(Create(wave_red), FadeIn(strawberry)),
                AnimationGroup(Create(wave_green), FadeIn(banana)),
                AnimationGroup(Create(wave_blue), FadeIn(blueberry)),
                lag_ratio=0.5
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Final emphasis on decomposition
        self.play(
            decomposition_text.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        # Grid positioning (Right half of the screen)
        start_x = 1.5
        end_x = 6.0
        start_y = 2.5
        end_y = -2.5

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Distribute points evenly in the right-side area
                pos_x = start_x + j * (end_x - start_x) / 5

            "- Essential for signal processing",
            "  and data compression."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Visualizing a complex wave and its decomposition
        # Sine wave components
        freq1, freq2 = 2, 5
        axes = Axes(

            x_length=4,

        f_axes = Axes(

        spike1 = Line(f_axes.c2p(freq1, 0), f_axes.c2p(freq1, 0.5), color=YELLOW)

        f_label = Text("Frequency Spectrum", font_size=18).next_to(f_axes, UP)

        self.play(Create(f_axes), Write(f_label))
        self.play(GrowFromEdge(spike1, DOWN), GrowFromEdge(spike2, DOWN))
        self.wait(2)

        # Highlight connection
        arrow = Arrow(axes.get_bottom(), f_axes.get_top(), color=GREY_A)
        ft_text = Text("Fourier Transform", font_size=16, color=BLUE).next_to(arrow, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(ft_text))
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data and setup
        title_str = "Dual Perspectives: Time vs. Frequency Domain"
        lines = [
            "The time domain shows signals wiggling over time.",
            "The frequency domain reveals the hidden notes within.",
            "It is like hearing music versus seeing sheet music."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        # Colors
        time_color = "#FFFFFF"
        freq_color = "#00FFFF"
        piano_color = "#E0E0E0"
        glow_color = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(time_color))

        # Time Domain Setup
        time_label = Text("Time Domain", font_size=24, color=time_color)
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, "A2")
        
        time_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY},
            x_length=3, y_length=2
        )
        self.place_in_area(time_axes, "B1", "C3")

        # Frequency Domain Setup
        freq_label = Text("Frequency Domain", font_size=24, color=freq_color)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, "A5")
        
        freq_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY},
            x_length=3, y_length=2
        )
        self.place_in_area(freq_axes, "B4", "C6")

        # Piano visualization
        piano_keys = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.3, height=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=WHITE, stroke_color=BLACK)
            for _ in range(7)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        self.place_in_area(piano_keys, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Single Sine Wave
        freq1 = 2
        sine_wave = time_axes.plot(lambda t: np.sin(2 * PI * freq1 * t / 4), color=time_color)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(time_label), FadeIn(time_axes),
            FadeIn(freq_label), FadeIn(freq_axes),
            Create(piano_keys)
        )
        
        self.play(
            piano_keys[2].animate.set_fill(piano_color), # Middle key highlight
            Create(sine_wave)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(freq_color)
        )

        # Single Spike
        spike1 = freq_axes.get_vertical_line(freq_axes.c2p(freq1, 1), color=freq_color)
        spike_dot = Dot(freq_axes.c2p(freq1, 1), color=freq_color, radius=0.05)
        spike_group = VGroup(spike1, spike_dot)

        self.play(Create(spike_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(glow_color)
        )

        # Three frequencies
        freq2 = 5
        freq3 = 8
        
        # Complex wave: sum of 3 sines
        complex_wave = time_axes.plot(
            lambda t: (np.sin(2 * PI * freq1 * t / 4) + 
                       0.5 * np.sin(2 * PI * freq2 * t / 4) + 
                       0.3 * np.sin(2 * PI * freq3 * t / 4)) / 1.8, 
            color=time_color
        )

        # Spikes
        spike2_line = freq_axes.get_vertical_line(freq_axes.c2p(freq2, 0.5), color=freq_color)
        spike2_dot = Dot(freq_axes.c2p(freq2, 0.5), color=freq_color, radius=0.05)
        spike3_line = freq_axes.get_vertical_line(freq_axes.c2p(freq3, 0.3), color=freq_color)
        spike3_dot = Dot(freq_axes.c2p(freq3, 0.3), color=freq_color, radius=0.05)
        
        all_spikes = VGroup(spike_group, VGroup(spike2_line, spike2_dot), VGroup(spike3_line, spike3_dot))

        self.play(
            piano_keys[0].animate.set_fill(piano_color),
            piano_keys[5].animate.set_fill(piano_color),
            Transform(sine_wave, complex_wave),
            FadeIn(all_spikes[1]),
            FadeIn(all_spikes[2])
        )
        
        # Glowing effect
        self.play(
            all_spikes.animate.set_color(glow_color),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(all_spikes, color=glow_color, scale_factor=1.2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        title_text = "The Mechanism: The 'Wrapping' Visualization"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Wrap signal around circle.", 
            "Center stays near origin.", 
            "Match frequency, things change.", 
            "Signal bunches, pulling center.", 
            "Shift creates chart peak."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        PINK_COLOR = "#FF00FF"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        YELLOW_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Positioning center using the area A1-F6
        origin_proxy = Dot(radius=0, color=BLACK)
        self.place_in_area(origin_proxy, "A1", "F6")
        center_pos = origin_proxy.get_center()

        # Signal properties
        SIGNAL_FREQ = 2.0
        f_wind_tracker = ValueTracker(0.4)
        
        # Wrapped signal
        wrapped_signal = VMobject(color=PINK_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        def get_wrapped_points(f_wind):
            # Sample density sufficient for smooth curves
            t_vals = np.linspace(0, 4.0, 400)
            # s(t) = offset signal to ensure center of mass shift
            s_t = (np.cos(2 * np.pi * SIGNAL_FREQ * t_vals) + 1.3) * 0.6
            # Polar conversion centered at center_pos
            # Clockwise winding (negative frequency)
            x = center_pos[0] + s_t * np.cos(-2 * np.pi * f_wind * t_vals)
            y = center_pos[1] + s_t * np.sin(-2 * np.pi * f_wind * t_vals)
            return [np.array([px, py, 0]) for px, py in zip(x, y)]

        # Initialize points
        wrapped_signal.set_points_as_corners(get_wrapped_points(f_wind_tracker.get_value()))
        
        # Performance: Use add_updater on persistent objects
        wrapped_signal.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_wrapped_points(f_wind_tracker.get_value())))

        # Center of Mass
        com_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        com_dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(np.mean(wrapped_signal.get_points(), axis=0)))

        # Peak Vector Arrow
        peak_vector = Arrow(
            start=center_pos, 
            end=center_pos + UP*0.1, 
            buff=0, 
            color=YELLOW_COLOR, 
            stroke_width=4,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        # Using put_start_and_end_on for performance
        peak_vector.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(center_pos, com_dot.get_center()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Wrap signal around circle
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PINK_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(wrapped_signal), run_time=2.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Center stays near origin
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(com_dot))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Match frequency, things change
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PINK_COLOR))
        # Transition frequency upwards towards resonance
        self.play(f_wind_tracker.animate.set_value(1.4), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Signal bunches, pulling center

        # Shift creates chart peak
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW_COLOR))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the scene layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Practical Magic: Noise Cancellation", 
            [
                'Real-world signals often contain unwanted noise.', 
                'The Fourier Transform identifies noise as specific spikes.', 
                'Deleting these spikes recovers the original clean signal.'
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_NOISY = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_FT_BOX = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_NOISE_SPIKE = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_CLEAN = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_NOISY)
        
        # Time Domain Axes
        axes_time = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_time, "B1", "F6")
        
        # Noisy wave: Signal (sin x) + High freq noise
        noisy_wave = axes_time.plot(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * 0.5 * x) + 0.2 * np.sin(2 * PI * 5 * x),
            color=COLOR_NOISY
        )
        time_label = Text("Time Domain", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, "B3")

        self.play(Create(axes_time), Write(time_label))
        self.play(Create(noisy_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_FT_BOX)
        
        # FT Box
        ft_box_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=COLOR_FT_BOX)
        ft_text = Text("Fourier Transform", font_size=16, color=COLOR_FT_BOX)
        ft_box = VGroup(ft_box_rect, ft_text)
        self.place_at_grid(ft_box, "A4")

        self.play(FadeIn(ft_box))
        
        # Frequency Domain Axes (Replace Time Axes content)
        axes_freq = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_freq, "B1", "F6")
        freq_label = Text("Frequency Domain", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, "B3")

        # Represent peaks as bars/spikes
        signal_peak = Line(
            axes_freq.c2p(1, 0), axes_freq.c2p(1, 1), 
            color=COLOR_CLEAN, stroke_width=6
        )
        noise_peak = Line(
            axes_freq.c2p(8, 0), axes_freq.c2p(8, 0.4), 
            color=COLOR_NOISE_SPIKE, stroke_width=6
        )
        noise_text = Text("Noise", font_size=18, color=COLOR_NOISE_SPIKE)
        self.place_at_grid(noise_text, "C5") # Positioned near noise_peak

        # Animation: Transition from time wave to frequency plot
        self.play(
            noisy_wave.animate.scale(0.1).move_to(ft_box.get_center()).set_opacity(0),
            FadeOut(time_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(axes_time, axes_freq),
            Write(freq_label),
            Create(signal_peak),
            Create(noise_peak),
            Write(noise_text)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_CLEAN)
        
        # Delete noise spike
        self.play(
            FadeOut(noise_peak),
            FadeOut(noise_text),
            noise_peak.animate.scale(0),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Conversion back to clean wave
        clean_wave = axes_time.plot(
            lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * 0.5 * x),
            color=COLOR_CLEAN
        )
        
        # Transform frequency plot back to time domain
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ft_box),
            FadeOut(freq_label),
            FadeOut(signal_peak),
            ReplacementTransform(axes_freq, axes_time),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Create(clean_wave),
            Write(time_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Fourier Transform: Decoding the DNA of Waves
outline.target_audience: University students in STEM fields (Engineering, Physics, or Math)

sections.title: The Smoothie Analogy: Deconstruction
sections.content: Introduce the core philosophy of the Fourier Transform: that any complex signal is just a combination of simpler parts. Use a culinary analogy to make the abstract concrete.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Magic Smoothie Machine.' You pour in a finished smoothie (the complex signal), and the machine separates it back into individual piles of strawberries, bananas, and blueberries (the pure frequencies). The Fourier Transform is that machine for math.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Sine Wave
sections.content: Briefly review the building blocks: Sine waves. Ensure the audience understands that a wave is defined by its amplitude (height) and frequency (speed of oscillation).
sections.example: Show a character, 'Sina the Snake,' slithering in a perfect wave. If she slithers faster, the frequency increases; if she jumps higher, the amplitude increases. We will prove that many 'Sinas' together can form any shape.

sections.title: Dual Perspectives: Time vs. Frequency Domain
sections.content: Introduce the shift in perspective. The 'Time Domain' shows what happens over time (a wiggly line), while the 'Frequency Domain' shows which notes are playing (a bar chart or spikes).
sections.example: Visualize a piano player. The 'Time Domain' is the recording of the song. The 'Frequency Domain' is the sheet music itself, showing exactly which keys (frequencies) were pressed and how hard (amplitude).

sections.title: The Mechanism: The 'Wrapping' Visualization
sections.content: Explain the mathematical process of 'winding' a signal around a circle at different frequencies. When the winding frequency matches the signal's frequency, the 'center of mass' shifts away from the origin.
sections.example: Animate a neon-colored wire (the signal) being wound around a spinning wheel. If the wheel spins at a random speed, the wire forms a messy, centered blob. But when the wheel spins at the 'magic frequency' of the signal, the wire bunched up on one side, making the graph 'peak' at that frequency.

sections.title: Practical Magic: Noise Cancellation
sections.content: Demonstrate a real-world application of the Fourier Transform: filtering unwanted data by identifying and removing specific frequency spikes.
sections.example: A recording of a 'Whistling Robot' has a high-pitched hum in the background. We use the Fourier Transform to find the specific 'hum spike,' erase it from the frequency chart, and transform it back into clean, hum-free audio.

storyboard.title: The Smoothie Analogy: Deconstruction
lecture_lines: Imagine a smoothie made of many different fruits.
It looks complex, but it is just a mixture.
The Fourier Transform is a magic deconstruction machine.
It separates the smoothie back into individual fruit piles.
It decomposes complex signals into simple waves.
animations: A complex, multi-frequency wave scrolls across the screen in #FFFFFF.
A rectangular box labeled 'Fourier Machine' (#FFFF00) appears; the complex wave flows into it.
Three pure sine waves (Red #FF0000, Green #00FF00, Blue #0000FF) emerge from the right side of the machine.
Three fruit icons (strawberry, banana, blueberry) appear next to their respective sine waves to represent ingredients.
The text 'Decomposition' in #00FFFF fades in above the machine to summarize the process.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Sine Wave
lecture_lines: Meet Sina the Snake, slithering in a perfect wave.
Slither speed represents the wave's frequency.
Jump height represents the wave's amplitude.
animations: A single green sine wave (#00FF00) representing a snake [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/snake.svg] slithers from left to right across the center of the screen.
The wave's vertical height expands and contracts; a vertical arrow and the label 'Amplitude' (#FF00FF) appear.
The wave's oscillations compress horizontally to show speed; the label 'Frequency' (#FFFF00) appears.

storyboard.title: Dual Perspectives: Time vs. Frequency Domain
lecture_lines: Split-screen shows time versus frequency perspectives.
A single note produces a simple sine wave.
In the frequency domain, it is one spike.
Combined notes form a complex, layered signal.
Spikes reveal every hidden ingredient in the mix.
animations: A split-screen view appears with 'Time Domain' (#FFFFFF) on the left and 'Frequency Domain' (#00FFFF) on the right.
A piano key [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/piano.svg] (#E0E0E0) is struck, showing a sine wave on the left and a single spike on the right.
Three keys [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/piano.svg] are struck, showing a complex wave on the left and three glowing spikes (#FFFF00) on the right.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: The 'Wrapping' Visualization
lecture_lines: Wrap signal around circle.
Center stays near origin.
Match frequency, things change.
Signal bunches, pulling center.
Shift creates chart peak.
animations: A pink signal wave (#FF00FF) begins to wrap around a central origin point in a circular motion.
The winding frequency starts low; the wrapped signal forms a centered, chaotic-looking blob.
A white dot (#FFFFFF) representing the center of mass is shown hovering near the origin.
The winding frequency increases to match the signal's frequency; the blob 'bunches up' on one side of the origin.
A vector arrow (#FFFF00) from the origin to the center of mass grows significantly, marking a frequency peak.

storyboard.title: Practical Magic: Noise Cancellation
lecture_lines: Real-world signals often contain unwanted noise.
The Fourier Transform identifies noise as specific spikes.
Deleting these spikes recovers the original clean signal.
animations: A jagged, noisy wave (#FFFFFF) is displayed, representing a signal with interference.
A 'Fourier Transform' box (#FFFF00) appears; the noisy wave enters and becomes a frequency plot.
On the frequency plot, a high-frequency spike is highlighted in red (#FF0000) and labeled 'Noise'.
The red noise spike (#FF0000) is deleted from the plot, leaving only the clean signal peak.
The frequency plot converts back into a smooth, clean green sine wave (#00FF00) in the time domain.
